points: Q3 will reveal whether the FirstFleet integration and Dedicated growth extended Q2's 80 bps adjusted operating margin improvement; further expansion supports the long case that the acquisition is delivering ahead of schedule.
The print will show if One-Way Truckload's strongest-in-a-decade revenue-per-truck momentum carried through the summer and whether restructuring gains can keep outpacing spot-market swings.

Werner Logistics posted a Q2 adjusted operating loss of $2.7 million versus prior-year income of $5.9 million; Q3 will reveal whether the segment is stabilizing and moving back toward profitability, a key lever for consolidated margins.

Q2 was the second consecutive quarter of favorable safety, insurance and claims trends; Q3 results will show if those cost tailwinds continued and helped convert revenue growth into operating leverage.

Reports suggest management sees driver attrition as only in the third inning and is optimistic about crackdowns on shadow capacity; Q3 commentary and Q4 guidance will indicate whether these capacity-tightening tailwinds are translating into firmer pricing and volumes.

Consensus already embeds FY1 EPS of $1.07 and FY2 EPS of $2.18, implying more than 100% growth next year; the Q3 print and any guidance update will test whether the CEO's 'accelerated earnings power' is on track to meet those steep expectations.
ODFL, MRTN and HTLD report within days of WERN, so their Q3 pricing, volume and margin read-throughs will either confirm or challenge the capacity-tightening thesis right around WERN's print.
watch: Adjusted operating margin: expands or holds above Q2's 3.0% — supports the long.
TTS revenue per truck: stays at or above Q2's decade-high growth pace — supports the long.
Werner Logistics adjusted operating result: loss narrows or returns to profit — supports the long.
Adjusted diluted EPS trajectory: Q3 result and guidance keep the FY1 $1.07 / FY2 $2.18 consensus path intact — supports the long.
